records.description: Pairwise scenario combinations under the `build` operation that no declarative case covers. The count is deliberately NOT restated here: `coverage report` recomputes it on every run and writes it to `target/conformance/coverage-pairwise.md`, which is the authoritative live number; a count copied into this description drifts silently the moment a case lands and makes the record read as worse (or better) than reality. This is missing COVERAGE, not missing representation: the pairs are enumerated and valid, and no program, waiver, or argument stands behind the uncovered ones. Each authored case re-dispositions the pairs it covers from this gap to `case` (flip the `odp-cmb-*` records in the same commit, or the report keeps counting a hole that is filled); this record is deleted once none remain.

deacon rejects a `features` map whose keys resolve to one canonical Feature id; the pinned spec defines both entries as distinct Features (feature-dependencies.md §Definition: Feature Equality), supplies an oldest-tag-first tie-break for exactly this collision (§Definition: Round Stable Sort), and states that "a single Feature may be installed more than once" (§Feature authorship). Oracle 0.87.0 resolves both digests in installOrder. This is an implementation gap rather than a coverage gap: the behavior is fully characterized on both sides and covered by case-readconfig-duplicate-feature-one-document-rejected — what is missing is the CAPABILITY, because deacon keys Feature identity version-independently (feature_resolver.rs sets id from the Feature metadata id, and the up staging maps in features_build.rs key on it), so simply deleting the parse-time rejection converts a loud error into a SILENT DROP of the second Feature, which is worse. Verified: with the validation removed, a real up fetched only git:1.3.1, staged one directory and emitted one feature RUN stage, exiting 0. Resolving this gap means making Feature identity per-entry, then re-recording the behavior and deleting this record in the same change.
